This has already been happening for years now. Here is another article on it. The most interesting thing about automation is that when successful it's mostly invisible. The biggest example is in the stock market. Now around 75% of all trades in the stock market are decided on, placed, and filled by AIs. Those AI started as little more than 'tools' to help out the human - much like in how this case the AI is just assisting the staff by reporting on something that's not receiving sufficient coverage - yet as the AI starts to approach the competence of the humans, the humans suddenly and instantly become redundant.

This is why I always speak of automation as a present day thing. There is some imminent automation that will be very visible and disruptive, like in fast food or driving and transportation, but most of it is just slowly absorbing jobs and is mostly invisible even if it is playing a meaningful part in the constant "Big company Y to lay of x,xxx workers." headlines we're constantly seeing now a days.

That's why I'm currently in the process of studying/switching careers to coding, AI/"big data ". The writing's on the wall, at this point.

If you want a stable future you'll either be programming the machines, building them, or maintaining them. Unskilled labor and even lower-level information work is rapidly becoming obsolete.

If you want a stable future

I was asctually counting on the machines doing everything, while we lay back in the sun with a chilled drink, except for the unlucky few who had to maintain these machines.

It's also a really fun career! AI is great stuff with basically infinite potential. A part of the project I'm currently working on is using substantial (though basic - expert system is the technical term) AI and it's often amazing seeing the output. And that's in an expert system where you have a pretty good idea about what's going on. Get into deep learning systems where the developers no longer have any clue what the AI is 'thinking' and the whole field is just great stuff. I demoed an alpha version to a friend who knows nothing about tech and he was stupefied that I had written all of the output. And of course I hadn't. He just had trouble grasping that it wasn't me formulating it, but the AI using a basic grammar and data analysis.

The more you learn about AI though the more it makes it feel like humanity really is just basically a boot loader for machine intelligence though. When I say their potential is infinite, I mean that quite literally. We're probably still many decades away from it, but goal oriented AI programming other AI to achieve abstract goals is completely within the realm of reality. It may even happen within our lifetimes given the exponential acceleration of tech behind the field.

The good news: AI will create more jobs than it destroys.

The good news (if you're an AI): Those jobs will all go to AIs.
